manifest.research_question: Research verified literature where user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry and generative semantic IDs intersect.

sources.title: HypRQ-VAE: Hyperbolic Item Indexing for Long-Tail-Aware Generative Recommender Systems
sources.exact_overlap: Strongest apparent intersection: explicitly combines hyperbolic-space item indexing with a residual-quantized VAE for generative recommendation, motivated by sequential recommendation and users' niche/long-tail preferences. The indexed metadata and abstract establish those themes, but do not establish that its evaluated task is specifically autoregressive user next-item prediction using generated semantic IDs; therefore it is not confirmed as a full three-way match.
sources.verified_metadata: OpenAlex work record and arXiv identifier/title agree; OpenAlex lists the arXiv PDF as an open full-text location.

sources.title: Generative Next POI Recommendation with Semantic ID
sources.exact_overlap: Directly addresses next-POI prediction from user preferences and historical check-ins, and proposes a generative semantic-ID representation constructed with residual quantization. No hyperbolic geometry is indicated in the abstract or indexed metadata, so this is a two-way behavior + generative-SID match, not the requested intersection.
sources.verified_metadata: OpenAlex record supplies DOI, title, abstract and an ACM PDF URL listed as full text.

sources.title: Hyperbolic Hypergraphs for Sequential Recommendation
sources.exact_overlap: Sequential recommendation from interaction histories is modeled with hyperbolic geometry and multi-scale sequence information. The abstract does not describe generative semantic IDs; this is a behavior + hyperbolic-geometry comparator, not a three-way match.
sources.verified_metadata: OpenAlex record supplies DOI, title, abstract and ACM PDF URL listed as full text.

sources.title: HMamba: Hyperbolic Mamba for Sequential Recommendation
sources.exact_overlap: Models user preference evolution from interaction sequences using hyperbolic geometry and a Mamba sequential recommender. No semantic-ID generation is indicated in the abstract; this is a behavior + hyperbolic-geometry comparator only.
sources.verified_metadata: OpenAlex record and arXiv identifier/title agree; OpenAlex lists the arXiv PDF as open full text.

sources.title: Hyperbolic Multi-semantic Transition for Next POI Recommendation
sources.exact_overlap: Explicitly predicts users' next POI from check-in mobility patterns and models multi-semantic transitions in hyperbolic space. No generative semantic IDs are described in the abstract; behavior + hyperbolic comparator only.
sources.verified_metadata: OpenAlex record supplies DOI, title, abstract and ACM PDF URL listed as full text.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Long-tail user intent / niche preference prediction
behavior_problem_candidates.basis: HypRQ-VAE frames head-versus-tail item imbalance and niche user preferences as a challenge for generative recommenders; its abstract motivates hyperbolic item indexing as a fit for power-law interactions.
behavior_problem_candidates.caveat: The available abstract does not establish sequence-conditioned next-item generation as the evaluated objective. Treat this as a problem candidate, not a verified finding about next-item behavior.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Semantic generalization in next-POI prediction from historical check-ins
behavior_problem_candidates.basis: GNPR-SID identifies random numeric POI IDs as limiting semantic relationships and constructs semantic IDs from collaborative and semantic features for generative next-POI recommendation.
behavior_problem_candidates.caveat: This source does not establish a hyperbolic representation.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Hierarchical and multi-timescale structure in sequential user behavior
behavior_problem_candidates.basis: H2SeqRec and HMamba motivate hyperbolic representations for hierarchical structure in sequential recommendation; HMST applies hyperbolic geometry to next-POI transition semantics.
behavior_problem_candidates.caveat: These works do not establish generative semantic-ID decoding.

limitations: No independently verified source in this search establishes all three elements together: user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry, and generative semantic IDs. HypRQ-VAE is the nearest apparent intersection, but the available evidence does not resolve whether next-item prediction with generated SIDs is its precise task.

Evidence labels are ABSTRACT because claims above were checked against indexed abstracts and metadata, not by reading and verifying the papers' body text. PDF/full-text URLs indicate discoverable full-text locations; they are not a claim that the full text was inspected.

FULL_TEXT means inspected full-text evidence; no source is assigned that label here. UNKNOWN would mean the relevant feature could not be determined from accessible evidence; where the abstract affirmatively omits a feature, it is described as not indicated rather than asserted absent from the entire paper.
OpenAlex was used for discovery and cross-checking bibliographic metadata/open-access locations; this is a targeted search, not an exhaustive systematic review.
